records.prompt: How should Shopify fashion brands prepare AI on-model product photos for a Shopify product page launch?
records.answerText:
Shopify fashion brands should prepare **clean, consistent source images**, define **brand-specific prompts and model rules**, and make sure the generated photos are reviewed for **fit accuracy, realism, and Shopify-ready formatting** before launch.[1][2][6]

For a product-page launch, the most effective prep is usually:

- **Start with strong garment inputs**: upload clear flat lays, packshots, mannequin shots, or basic model images so the AI has a reliable reference to place the clothing on a model.[1][2][6]
- **Standardize the look**: decide in advance on model gender presentation, body type, pose style, background, and lighting so the imagery stays consistent across the catalog and campaign set.[1][3][7]
- **Use detailed prompts**: if the tool supports text prompting, include specifics like pose, setting, ethnicity, hair, and mood to keep outputs aligned with the brand aesthetic.[1][4]
- **Check product fidelity**: verify that seams, logos, prints, proportions, drape, and color remain faithful to the real garment, since AI fashion tools are meant to convert product shots into on-model visuals, not redesign the item.[2][6]
- **Create a launch set, not just one hero image**: prepare a mix of hero images, close-ups, lifestyle views, and if available short videos so the product page feels complete and conversion-oriented.[4][5][6]
- **Publish in a Shopify-compatible workflow**: choose outputs that can be attached directly to products or product feeds so you can update images quickly and keep inventory pages synchronized.[2][6]
- **Lock in repeatable brand assets**: if the platform offers model consistency or reusable digital-twin style outputs, save the approved model/look so future collections match the same visual identity.[1][3]

A practical launch workflow is: **prepare source garment photos → generate several on-model variations → select the most accurate and on-brand versions → optimize crop/size for Shopify → attach them to the product page → test the page on mobile before going live**.[2][4][6]
